**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [c-Fos (Npas4) + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for whole mouse brain clearing due to its high fluorescence preservation, compatibility with lipid-soluble dyes, and ability to maintain fine cellular structures. The use of c-Fos (Npas4) as a marker for activated neurons combined with DAPI for nuclear labeling allows for single-cell resolution imaging. This method supports long-term sample stability and is compatible with light-sheet microscopy, ideal for generating 3D distribution maps.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with 1:500 anti-c-Fos (Npas4) antibody in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 1:500 Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated secondary antibody in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 1:1000 DAPI in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI, e.g., 10% (vol/vol) polyethylene glycol 350, 10% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol, 80% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Sample Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer the cleared brain into a glass-bottom dish filled with RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: ongoing)  
5.2 Store at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging  
5.3 For imaging, ensure the brain is fully immersed in RI-matching solution and mounted on a light-sheet or confocal microscope platform.

1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48, e.g., 1.48 RI oil or custom mix of DBE and benzyl alcohol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4.2 Incubation with primary antibody against MBP (1:500 dilution in blocking buffer) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500 dilution in blocking buffer) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with NeuroTrace 530/615 (1:1000 dilution in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 dilution in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  

5 Wash

5.2 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Final RI Matching and Storage

MBP (myelin basic protein) is a key marker for mature myelinated axons, allowing visualization of residual myelinated structures and regenerated fibers. The combination of DiI (for tracing regenerating or newly formed axons) and MBP (for assessing myelination and continuity of existing axons) provides complementary information on both regeneration and survival. iDISCO+'s organic solvent-based clearing also allows for deep penetration and compatibility with long-term imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with DiI (1 µg/mL in 100% methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Washing with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with MBP antibody (1:200 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
2.4 Washing with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.6 Washing with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI, e.g., 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, MBP]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for long-range imaging of whole CNS tissues due to its high fluorescence preservation, compatibility with lipid-soluble dyes like DiI, and ability to clear large tissue samples (up to 40 mm in length). The use of DiI allows for tracing of long axonal projections from the cortex to the spinal cord, while MBP (myelin basic protein) provides a reference signal for identifying white matter tracts. This combination enables visualization of both target projection fibers and the surrounding myelinated pathways, facilitating analysis of spatial overlap and branching patterns.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with DiI (1 µg/mL in 100% methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)  
2.2 Incubation with MBP antibody (1:500 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)  
2.3 Washing with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI, e.g., dibenzyl ether or custom RI solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Mounting in RI-matching solution within a glass-bottomed dish or custom chamber for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

2.2 Incubation with 1:100 Claudin-5 antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 647, Claudin-5 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for large tissue blocks (up to several cm³), provides excellent fluorescence preservation, and allows for deep penetration of fluorescent signals, which is critical for visualizing fine vascular structures and barrier components like Claudin-5 in 3D. The use of CD31 (for endothelial cells) and Claudin-5 (for blood-brain barrier integrity) enables precise analysis of vascular continuity and barrier disruption in tumor core, invasive front, and normal brain regions.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA + 10% NGS in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CD31 (1:100 dilution in blocking solution) and anti-Claudin-5 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS + 0.1% Tween-20) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) × 3 times  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS + 0.1% Tween-20) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) × 3 times  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 10% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran, 80% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 RI Matching and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with refractive index matching solution (RI = 1.48, e.g., 1.48 RI oil or custom mix of glycerol and water) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with refractive index matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with refractive index matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.3 Incubation with 1 µg/mL DAPI in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

目前该类样本在透明化和保存后容易出现报告荧光进一步衰减、背景升高或树突细节丢失，导致长期归档后难以复查。请根据上述科学目标，在不引入给定标记物列表之外靶点或表外荧光团的前提下，重新选择或调整荧光/标记策略与组织透明方法，使其适合弱内源荧光保留、树突结构补全、3 mm 厚脑组织块透明化和 6 个月长期保存。
请仅输出修正后的 protocol，第 1 行写明应保留或更换的双靶点荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-suited for thick brain tissues (up to 3 mm) and provides excellent optical transparency while preserving weak endogenous fluorescence signals. It uses organic solvents that are compatible with a wide range of fluorescent proteins and dyes, including GFP and Alexa Fluor 647. The use of MAP2 and Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 allows for detailed reconstruction of neuronal morphology, including dendritic arborization and cytoskeletal structures, which is critical for analyzing cell body position, dendritic branching, and local projection patterns. The method also supports long-term storage in refractive index-matched media without significant signal degradation over 6 months.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with 1:500 dilution of MAP2 antibody in 1× PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 1:200 dilution of Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 in 1× PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.3 Washing with 1× PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)  

5 Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 10% (vol/vol) NMP, 80% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 20% (vol/vol) NMP, 60% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (40% (vol/vol) DMSO, 40% (vol/vol) NMP, 20% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.4 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (60% (vol/vol) DMSO, 60% (vol/vol) NMP) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI-matching medium (1.48 RI, e.g., dibenzyl ether or uDISCO RI-matching solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with RI-matching medium (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

7 Storage/Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer tissue to fresh RI-matching medium and store at 4 ℃ for up to 6 months  
7.2 For imaging, ensure the tissue is fully immersed in RI-matching medium and mounted in a low-auto-fluorescent chamber or cuvette suitable for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3), MAP2]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for thick human brain tissue due to its high penetration of fluorescently labeled antibodies and excellent optical clarity, enabling deep imaging. It uses organic solvents that are compatible with lipid-soluble dyes and allows for long-term antibody incubation at 4°C, which is critical for antigen detection in fixed human tissue. NeuN and MAP2 are robust markers for mature neurons and their somata, respectively, and can be reliably detected with commercial antibodies. Using two independent markers increases the reliability of identifying mature neurons across the entire thickness of the 3 mm slice.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with 1% (wt/vol) BSA in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail (NeuN, 1:500; MAP2, 1:500) in 1% BSA/methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 1% (wt/vol) BSA in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail (Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG, 1:500; Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG, 1:500) in 1% BSA/methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with 1% (wt/vol) BSA in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (1:1 DBE:refractive index matching gel, e.g., RIM-1000) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Mounting in RI matching gel for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed)

**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is a rapid, organic solvent-based clearing method that provides excellent optical transparency and fluorescence preservation, particularly suitable for thick brain slices (up to 500 μm). It avoids the use of methanol, which can cause tissue shrinkage and damage to delicate structures like dendritic spines. GFP is ideal for sparse labeling of neurons, while Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 labels F-actin in dendrites and spines, enabling high-resolution visualization of dendritic architecture and spine density without introducing additional fluorescent targets.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) tert-butyl alcohol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) tert-butyl alcohol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) tert-butyl alcohol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert-butyl alcohol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM again (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with uDISCO mounting medium (RI = 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with uDISCO mounting medium again (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.2 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) to remove excess dye  
2.3 Incubation with 100% DMSO (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) to dissolve DiI  
2.4 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) to wash out residual DMSO

The use of DiI and DiO allows dual-color labeling of distinct neural populations, enhancing the ability to distinguish and track different cranial, spinal, and peripheral nerve tracts in a single specimen.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with DiI (1 µg/mL in 100% methanol) for 2 days (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with DiO (1 µg/mL in 100% methanol) for 2 days (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

2.6 Washing with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.7 Washing with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

The use of Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82), a presynaptic active zone marker, and Synapsin, a presynaptic vesicle-associated protein, allows precise visualization of synaptic architecture and vesicle domains, aligning well with the goal of analyzing synaptic density and functional domains in Drosophila brain circuits.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.1 Incubation with primary antibody against Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) at 1:500 dilution in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (for BRP) and Alexa Fluor 594 (for Synapsin) at 1:500 dilution in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) + Alexa Fluor 488, Synaptotagmin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is specifically optimized for small insect brains like the *Drosophila* brain, including those with intact cuticle. It provides excellent optical clarity while preserving subcellular structures such as synaptic active zones and vesicles. The method uses a sequential dehydration and clearing process that is compatible with immunostaining using primary and secondary antibodies conjugated to fluorescent dyes. The use of Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 ensures good spectral separation for dual-channel imaging, and the labeling targets BRP (a marker for presynaptic active zones) and Synaptotagmin (a marker for synaptic vesicles), which aligns directly with the scientific goal of distinguishing different functional domains within synapses.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) at 1:50 dilution in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody Synaptotagmin at 1:50 dilution in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG at 1:200 dilution in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG at 1:200 dilution in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Washing with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)  

3 Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methyl salicylate (MS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) MS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) MS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 RI Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) refractive index matching solution (RI = 1.52, e.g., benzyl alcohol/benzyl benzoate, 1:1) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) RI matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) RI matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Preservation and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mounting in RI matching solution using a glass-bottomed dish or coverslip (Temperature: RT, Time: immediately before imaging)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osteocalcin (Osx), CD31]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard tissues like bone, providing excellent optical transparency while preserving fluorescent signals. It uses a sequential dehydration and delipidation process with organic solvents that are compatible with fluorescent markers. Osteocalcin (Osx) is a well-established marker for mature osteoblasts, while CD31 labels endothelial cells, enabling the visualization of vascular networks in the cranial suture region. This combination allows precise mapping of osteogenic lineage cells and their spatial relationship with blood vessels during postnatal bone formation.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert-butyl alcohol (TBA) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibody against Osteocalcin (1:100 dilution in TBA) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200 dilution in TBA) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with CD31 antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100 dilution in TBA) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Washing with TBA (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with BoneClear reagent (1:1 vol/vol TBA:BoneClear) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% BoneClear (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 RI Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., 50% w/v sorbitol in water) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mounting in RI-matched solution using a glass-bottomed dish or coverslip (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osteocalcin, Osx (Osterix) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard tissues like bone, offering effective clearing while preserving endogenous fluorescent signals and minimizing tissue deformation. It uses a sequential dehydration and refractive index matching approach that is compatible with fluorescent markers such as Osteocalcin (for mature osteoblasts) and Osx (for early osteoblast progenitors), which can be detected using specific antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647. This labeling strategy allows for dual-color detection of differentiating osteoblast populations without introducing additional fluorescent dyes that may increase background or interfere with imaging. The method also reduces bone autofluorescence through its clearing agents, improving signal-to-noise ratio for precise 3D localization.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: anti-Osteocalcin (1:200 dilution) and anti-Osx (1:200 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 1% BSA in PBS for washing (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) (Repeat 3 times)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) acetone (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) acetone (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with BoneClear reagent 1 (10% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with BoneClear reagent 2 (20% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with BoneClear reagent 3 (40% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol, 40% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with BoneClear reagent 4 (60% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol, 60% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.5 Incubation with BoneClear reagent 5 (80% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol, 80% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.6 Incubation with BoneClear reagent 6 (100% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol, 100% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 RI Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., dibenzyl ether or custom RI solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6.1 Incubation with 1% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde in RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) + CD31 (PECAM1) + Phalloidin]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for bone tissues, providing excellent optical transparency while preserving fluorescent signals. It uses a sequential dehydration and delipidation process with organic solvents that are compatible with fluorescent proteins and dyes commonly used in immunohistochemistry. TH labeling allows visualization of sympathetic nerve fibers, CD31 labels vascular endothelium, and Phalloidin stains F-actin in vascular structures and surrounding stroma, enabling the 3D analysis of spatial relationships between nerves, vessels, and the bone marrow microenvironment.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody against TH (1:500 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody against CD31 (1:200 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:100 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody (anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488, 1:500 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with secondary antibody (anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 568, 1:500 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Washing with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert-butyl alcohol (TBA) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) TBA (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) TBA (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with BoneClear RI matching solution (1.51 RI) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with BoneClear RI matching solution (1.51 RI) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) glycerol (RI = 1.47) to adjust refractive index for imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Mounting in a custom glass chamber or on a coverslip with refractive index-matched mounting medium (RI = 1.51) for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin (F-Actin), alpha-bungarotoxin (AChR), DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for clearing dense, mineralized tissues such as bone, making it ideal for the deeply embedded mouse cochlea. It provides excellent optical transparency while preserving fluorescent signals, which is critical for visualizing the fine structure of hair cells and their spatial organization. Phalloidin labels F-actin in hair cell stereocilia, alpha-bungarotoxin binds to nicotinic acetylcholine receptors on inner hair cells, and DAPI stains nuclei, enabling clear discrimination between inner and outer hair cells and their arrangement within the cochlear spiral. This labeling strategy avoids the need for additional antibodies, leveraging small molecule probes that are compatible with BoneClear.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with 1:100 Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 in 100% ethylene glycol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 1:500 alpha-bungarotoxin-Alexa Fluor 594 in 100% ethylene glycol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 1:1000 DAPI in 100% ethylene glycol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Washing with 100% ethylene glycol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48, e.g., 80% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Mounting the cleared cochlea in RI-matching solution (1.48) using a low-viscosity mounting medium (e.g., Prolong Glass Antifade Mountant)  
4.2 Cover with a glass coverslip and seal with nail polish or adhesive for long-term storage and imaging.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, Phalloidin, Hoechst]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-suited for small, hard tissues like teeth due to its organic solvent-based clearing that effectively reduces light scattering while preserving fine structures and fluorescence. It avoids the high-temperature steps of some methods, which can damage delicate neural structures. DiI labels lipid-rich structures such as nerve fibers, Phalloidin stains F-actin in soft tissue, and Hoechst highlights nuclei, providing a multi-scale view of the pulp chamber and nerve distribution without introducing extraneous markers.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with DiI (1 µg/mL in DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100 dilution in DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (1:1000 dilution in DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (10% (vol/vol) DCM, 10% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF), 80% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (20% (vol/vol) DCM, 20% (vol/vol) THF, 60% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (30% (vol/vol) DCM, 30% (vol/vol) THF, 40% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (40% (vol/vol) DCM, 40% (vol/vol) THF, 20% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.5 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (50% (vol/vol) DCM, 50% (vol/vol) THF) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 RI Matching  
5.1 Incubation with refractive index matching solution (RI = 1.51, e.g., benzyl alcohol/benzyl benzoate 1:1) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with 1% (vol/vol) Sudan Black B in RI matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) to reduce autofluorescence  
6.2 Mounting in RI matching solution on a glass slide with a coverslip for imaging (e.g., using a confocal or light-sheet microscope)

**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin (F-Actin), DiI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard tissues such as bone and cartilage, making it ideal for the spinal vertebrae-muscle composite tissue. It provides excellent optical transparency while preserving fluorescent signals, which is critical for visualizing both the fine peripheral nerve networks and the muscle fiber architecture. Phalloidin labels F-actin in muscle fibers, providing a structural reference, while DiI is an efficient lipophilic dye for labeling nerve fibers, allowing clear visualization of their branching patterns and spatial relationships with surrounding muscle structures.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of DiI in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Washing with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with BoneClear reagent (100% vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with BoneClear reagent (100% vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with BoneClear reagent (100% vol/vol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

5 RI Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., 50% w/v sorbitol in water) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with RI matching solution (1.51 RI) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with RI matching solution (1.51 RI) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mounting in RI matching solution (1.51 RI) using a low-viscosity optical mounting medium compatible with fluorescence imaging (e.g., refractive index 1.51)  
6.2 Cover with a glass coverslip and seal with nail polish or UV-curable adhesive to prevent evaporation  
6.3 Store at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging.

The use of DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining to distinguish individual cells and aid in segmentation during 3D reconstruction. This method also supports high-resolution imaging with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, aligning with the need for single-cell resolution.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing

1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with 1 µg/mL IB4 lectin in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 1 µg/mL CD31 antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (Alexa Fluor 647), CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly effective for clearing thick, pigmented tissues like melanoma due to its organic solvent-based approach, which efficiently removes lipids and melanin while preserving fluorescence. The use of Alexa Fluor 647 and 555 allows for red/ far-red channel imaging with high signal-to-noise ratio, suitable for deep tissue visualization. Lectin labels endothelial cell membranes, while CD31 marks vascular endothelium, enabling both structural and functional vascular analysis. DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for anatomical reference.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3 Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of Lectin (Alexa Fluor 647) in 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of anti-CD31 (PECAM1) antibody conjugated with Alexa Fluor 555 in 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of DAPI in 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Washing with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5 RI Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) refractive index matching solution (RI = 1.51, e.g., benzyl alcohol/benzyl benzoate, 1:1) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) RI matching solution (RI = 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Mounting in RI-matched solution for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19 (导管) + Alexa Fluor 488, E-cadherin + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for rapid clearing of small tissue blocks (<5 mm³), with excellent fluorescence preservation and compatibility with multiple fluorescent dyes. CK19 and E-cadherin are specific markers for epithelial cells, particularly ductal structures in breast cancer, enabling precise identification of residual cancer cells at the margin. DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for structural context. The organic solvent-based approach allows for fast processing within 24–48 hours, aligning with the time constraints of intraoperative or near-intraoperative assessment.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Incubation with 1% (wt/vol) BSA in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: CK19 (1:100 dilution in 1% BSA/PBS) and E-cadherin (1:200 dilution in 1% BSA/PBS) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:200 dilution in 1% BSA/PBS) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:200 dilution in 1% BSA/PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in 1% BSA/PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  

3 Wash  
3.1 Incubation with 1% (wt/vol) BSA in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ RI matching solution (1:1 ratio of dibenzyl ether (DBE) and 1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME)) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6.1 Incubation with 1% (vol/vol) Sudan Black B in DBE/DME mixture to reduce background autofluorescence (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh DBE/DME RI matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

Hoechst 33342 and Propidium Iodide provide nuclear staining for cell localization and differentiation between viable and necrotic regions, aiding in accurate interpretation of tumor margins.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Incubation with 1% (wt/vol) BSA in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody against CK19 (1:100 dilution in 1% BSA/PBS) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 1% (wt/vol) BSA in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200 dilution in 1% BSA/PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 1% (wt/vol) BSA in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Nuclear Staining  
3.1 Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (1:1000 dilution in 1% BSA/PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with Propidium Iodide (1:1000 dilution in 1% BSA/PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 1% (wt/vol) BSA in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a rapid, solvent-based clearing method that provides excellent fluorescence preservation and optical transparency for whole tissue blocks within 24–48 hours. It is particularly suitable for small to medium-sized tissues like the 5 mm × 5 mm × 3 mm breast biopsy block. The use of CK19 (a ductal epithelial marker) labeled with Alexa Fluor 647 allows specific identification of epithelial cancer nests, while DAPI serves as a nuclear counterstain for structural reference. This labeling strategy enables accurate 3D mapping of residual cancer foci near the surgical margin.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of anti-CK19 antibody in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 1:200 dilution of Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated secondary antibody in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of DAPI in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48, e.g., 10% (vol/vol) DBE in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) RI-matching solution (1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Mounting in RI-matching solution on a glass-bottom dish for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

1.7 Washing with PBS + 0.1% Tween-20 for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
1.8 Incubation with secondary antibody (if needed) or directly conjugated primary antibodies for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.9 Washing with PBS + 0.1% Tween-20 for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
1.10 Incubation with Phalloidin (Alexa Fluor 568, 1:100 dilution) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.11 Washing with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
1.12 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 dilution) for 10 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
1.13 Washing with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

我使用 FOCM 处理前列腺癌活检样本，但透明后腺体结构显示不清，且组织有明显收缩变形。此前流程包含甲醇脱水和 DBE 透明，可能导致针芯组织脱水过强、RI 变化过快和组织尺度收缩。请根据上述科学目标，在不引入给定标记物列表之外靶点或表外荧光团的前提下，重新选择或调整荧光/标记策略与组织透明方法。修正版应适合前列腺针芯活检组织的低形变透明化、癌变腺上皮与基底细胞层双信号检测、腺体结构保持和三维成像。

请仅输出修正后的 protocol，第 1 行写明应保留或更换的荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DAPI, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647, CK19 (导管), AQP1]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is a methanol-based clearing method that provides excellent fluorescence preservation and minimal tissue shrinkage, which is critical for maintaining the structural integrity of thin needle-core prostate tissues. It allows for long-term sample stability and compatibility with multiple fluorescent labels. DAPI labels nuclei, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 highlights F-actin in epithelial cells, CK19 marks ductal structures, and AQP1 labels the basal cell layer, enabling dual detection of cancerous epithelium and basal layer integrity. This labeling strategy avoids introducing new targets outside the provided list and supports 3D imaging of key Gleason score features.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of CK19 antibody in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of AQP1 antibody in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of DAPI in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Washing with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 10% (vol/vol) NMP, 80% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 20% (vol/vol) NMP, 60% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (40% (vol/vol) DMSO, 40% (vol/vol) NMP, 20% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 RI Matching  
5.1 Incubation with uDISCO RI matching solution (40% (vol/vol) DMSO, 40% (vol/vol) NMP, 20% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with uDISCO RI matching solution (60% (vol/vol) DMSO, 60% (vol/vol) NMP, 10% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with uDISCO RI matching solution (80% (vol/vol) DMSO, 80% (vol/vol) NMP, 10% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with uDISCO RI matching solution (100% (vol/vol) DMSO, 100% (vol/vol) NMP) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Mounting in uDISCO RI matching solution (100% (vol/vol) DMSO, 100% (vol/vol) NMP) for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for clearing small to medium-sized tissues like lymph nodes, offering excellent fluorescence preservation and compatibility with lipid-soluble dyes. It allows for deep penetration of fluorescent signals, which is essential for visualizing both HEV-specific addressin markers and the broader vascular endothelial network. The use of Hoechst 33342 provides a nuclear counterstain to assess lymphocyte distribution and cell density gradients. α-Actinin labeling helps delineate the general vascular endothelium, while HEV-specific addressin (e.g., Pgp-1/CD62L) enables distinction between HEV and other vascular structures.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: anti-CD62L (HEV addressin) at 1:100 dilution and anti-α-Actinin at 1:200 dilution in 1% BSA/PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:500) in 1% BSA/PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (1:1000 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM again (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.2 Incubation with fresh iDISCO+ RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Mounting on a glass slide with a coverslip using RI-matching solution for imaging (e.g., light-sheet or confocal microscopy).

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (Alexa Fluor 647), CD3 (PE), DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for small immune organs like lymph nodes due to its rapid clearing process, excellent fluorescence preservation, and compatibility with a wide range of fluorescent dyes. Lectin (Alexa Fluor 647) effectively labels high endothelial venules (HEVs), while CD3 (PE) marks T cells, allowing spatial analysis of lymphocyte distribution relative to HEVs. DAPI provides nuclear staining for identifying cell-dense regions. This labeling strategy enables precise 3D mapping of HEV networks and their interaction with immune cell zones.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.6 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated lectin (e.g., Peanut Agglutinin, PNA) in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 1:50 dilution of PE-conjugated anti-CD3 antibody in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Washing with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)

5 Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

6 RI Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) refractive index matching solution (e.g., RIM-1, RI = 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) RIM-1 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Mounting in RIM-1 on a glass-bottom dish for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

请根据该科学问题自行选择合适的荧光/标记策略，并匹配适合完整肿瘤免疫微环境成像的组织透明方法。若限制范围内的血管腔面探针或核染料能够提供血管/结构参考，可作为辅助信号；但不能替代 T 细胞亚群主标记。请仅输出 protocol，第 1 行写明所选荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD3 (Alexa Fluor 647), CD8 (Alexa Fluor 594), DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for whole-mount tissue imaging of intact tumors due to its high fluorescence preservation, compatibility with multiple fluorescent markers, and ability to clear large tissues (up to several cm³). The use of organic solvents allows for efficient lipid removal while maintaining antigenicity for immunostaining. CD3 and CD8 antibodies are ideal for distinguishing total T cells (CD3+) from cytotoxic T cells (CD8+), while DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for structural reference. This labeling strategy enables precise spatial mapping of immune cell infiltration patterns in the tumor microenvironment.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA + 10% normal goat serum in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CD3 (Alexa Fluor 647, 1:100 dilution) and anti-CD8 (Alexa Fluor 594, 1:100 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody (if needed, e.g., anti-rat Alexa Fluor 488, 1:200 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
2.5 Washing with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (10% (vol/vol) DCM, 10% (vol/vol) DBE, 80% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (20% (vol/vol) DCM, 20% (vol/vol) DBE, 60% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (30% (vol/vol) DCM, 30% (vol/vol) DBE, 40% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (40% (vol/vol) DCM, 40% (vol/vol) DBE, 20% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.5 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (50% (vol/vol) DCM, 50% (vol/vol) DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

5 RI Matching  
5.1 Incubation with refractive index matching solution (RI = 1.48, e.g., 1.48 RI oil or custom mix of DBE and glycerol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mounting the cleared tumor in RI-matching solution within a glass-bottomed dish or coverslip for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.  
6.2 Ensure the sample is fully immersed in RI-matching solution to minimize optical distortion during imaging.

我需要对小鼠皮下移植瘤进行透明化处理，用于定量分析肿瘤核心和边缘区域中 T 细胞浸润密度，以区分免疫“冷”肿瘤和“热”肿瘤。样本为完整皮下移植瘤，大小约 8 mm × 8 mm × 6 mm，已完成固定和后固定。科学目标是在三维空间中区分泛 T 细胞和细胞毒性 T 细胞亚群，比较它们在肿瘤边缘、肿瘤核心、血管周围区域和坏死区附近的浸润密度、分布深度和聚集模式。

请仅输出修正后的 protocol，第 1 行写明应保留或更换的荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Cx40 (Connexin 40) + Alexa Fluor 647, Cx43 (Connexin 43) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for whole organs like the mouse heart due to its high fluorescence preservation and compatibility with multiple fluorescent channels. It uses organic solvents that effectively clear tissues while maintaining signal integrity, which is critical for observing fine structures like Purkinje fibers and gap junctions. The labeling strategy includes specific antibodies against Cx40 and Cx43, which are key components of the conduction system, along with DAPI for nuclear counterstaining. This allows for dual-channel imaging of Purkinje fiber-associated contact proteins and gap junctions (Cx40/Cx43), enabling precise spatial analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) PBS-buffered methanol solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) PBS-buffered methanol solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) PBS-buffered methanol solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) PBS-buffered methanol solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) PBS-buffered methanol solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum in PBS-T) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: anti-Cx40 (1:200, rabbit IgG) + anti-Cx43 (1:200, goat IgG) in PBS-T (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) + Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:500) in PBS-T (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 in PBS-T) (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI, e.g., SeeDB2 or custom mix of 20% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol and 20% (vol/vol) benzyl benzoate in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Sample Preparation for Imaging  
5.1 Mounting the cleared heart in RI-matching solution within a glass-bottom dish or coverslip (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed)  
5.2 Imaging using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate excitation/emission settings for Alexa Fluor 488, 647, and DAPI.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 647, CD31+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for whole organ clearing of relatively large tissues like the mouse kidney, offering excellent fluorescence preservation and compatibility with multiple fluorescent labels. The use of organic solvents allows for efficient lipid removal while maintaining structural integrity and fluorescent signal. Nephrin labeling targets podocytes in glomeruli, CD31 identifies vascular endothelium (capillary loops), and DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for morphological context. This combination enables precise identification and quantification of glomerular structures in 3D.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: Nephrin (NPHS1) at 1:100 dilution + CD31 at 1:200 dilution in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Washing with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) repeated 3 times  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) + Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Washing with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) repeated 3 times  
2.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 μg/mL in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
2.7 Washing with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) repeated 2 times

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert-butyl alcohol (TBA) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (100% DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (100% DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (100% DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI, e.g., 1.48 RI glycerol-based solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mounting the cleared kidney in RI-matching solution within a glass-bottomed dish or custom chamber suitable for light-sheet microscopy  
6.2 Ensuring no air bubbles are present under the tissue  
6.3 Covering the sample with a coverslip or using an immersion objective for confocal imaging if needed

**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)-Alexa Fluor 647, Podocin (NPHS2)-Alexa Fluor 555, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for whole organs like the kidney due to its high transparency and excellent fluorescence preservation, especially for deep tissue imaging. It allows for long-term incubation with fluorescently labeled antibodies and phalloidin, which is critical for detecting both the structural integrity of glomeruli (via F-actin) and the two key podocyte slit diaphragm proteins (Nephrin and Podocin). The organic solvent-based clearing ensures uniform refractive index matching across the entire kidney, including cortex and medulla, addressing the issue of uneven transparency. This method also supports high-resolution light-sheet or confocal imaging for 3D reconstruction and quantification.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) PBS-buffered methanol (PB-MeOH) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) PB-MeOH (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) PB-MeOH (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) PB-MeOH (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) PB-MeOH (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA in PB-MeOH) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: Nephrin (NPHS1)-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:100 dilution), Podocin (NPHS2)-Alexa Fluor 555 (1:100 dilution) in PB-MeOH (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 1% BSA in PB-MeOH (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody (if needed, but not required here as primary is directly conjugated) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100 dilution) in PB-MeOH (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI, e.g., 20% (vol/vol) polyethylene glycol 300, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 70% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19 (导管), Lectin, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for whole organs like the liver due to its high penetration depth and excellent fluorescence preservation, which is critical for visualizing fine structures such as bile duct networks. The use of CK19 specifically labels biliary epithelial cells, while Lectin and IB4 can be used to mark vascular endothelium in portal areas, aiding in spatial correlation between bile ducts and portal tracts. DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for structural context. This method allows for long-term sample storage and compatibility with light-sheet microscopy, ideal for 3D reconstruction.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of anti-CK19 antibody in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated secondary antibody in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of FITC-conjugated Lectin in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of DAPI in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)

3 Wash  
3.1 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert-butyl alcohol (TBA) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) TBA (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) TBA (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5 Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (1:1:1 v/v/v of dibenzyl ether, tetrahydrofuran, and xylene) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6 RI Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 1:1 (v/v) iDISCO+ clearing solution and refractive index matching solution (RI = 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with 1:2 (v/v) iDISCO+ clearing solution and refractive index matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with 1:4 (v/v) iDISCO+ clearing solution and refractive index matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.4 Incubation with 1:8 (v/v) iDISCO+ clearing solution and refractive index matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.5 Incubation with pure refractive index matching solution (RI = 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of Hoechst 33342 in refractive index matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) for nuclear enhancement if needed  
7.2 Storage in refractive index matching solution at 4 ℃ until imaging.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Insulin (primary antibody, Alexa Fluor 647 conjugated), DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for clearing large, irregularly shaped tissues like the mouse pancreas, offering excellent fluorescence preservation and compatibility with multiple fluorescent labels. It uses organic solvents that are compatible with lipid-soluble dyes and antibodies, which is ideal for labeling β cells with an insulin-specific antibody and nuclei with DAPI. This method allows for high-resolution imaging of the entire pancreas, enabling accurate quantification of β cell volume and distribution without sampling bias.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of anti-Insulin primary antibody in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 1:200 dilution of Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated secondary antibody in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of DAPI in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE containing 0.1% (wt/vol) Sudan Black B to reduce background autofluorescence (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Mounting in DBE on a glass slide with a coverslip for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Insulin (primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 488), PDX1 (primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 647), DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-suited for whole organ clearing of soft tissues like the pancreas, offering excellent fluorescence preservation and minimal structural deformation. It uses organic solvents that are compatible with antibody-based labeling and allows for long-term preservation of antigenicity and fluorescent signals. The use of Insulin and PDX1 antibodies with Alexa Fluor conjugates enables dual-color detection of β-cell hormone and transcription factor, while DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for accurate quantification of β-cell volume, islet number, and distribution.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% BSA in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Insulin (1:100 dilution) and anti-PDX1 (1:200 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Washing with PBS-T (0.3% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 times)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-goat (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Washing with PBS-T (0.3% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 times)  
2.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 μg/mL in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
2.7 Washing with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 times)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert-butyl alcohol (TBA) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI, e.g., 10% (vol/vol) w/v sorbitol in DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with fresh RI-matching solution (1.48 RI) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Preservation and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) glycerol (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.5 Mounting in 100% glycerol on a glass slide for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

This labeling strategy supports high-resolution 3D imaging of neural distribution patterns in different anatomical regions of the fat pad.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA + 10% normal goat serum in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: TH (1:500, rabbit anti-TH, Abcam ab15239) + IB4 (1:100, IB4 biotinylated, Vector Laboratories B-1215) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) + streptavidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for permeabilization (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
