TH labeling effectively identifies sympathetic nerve fibers, while IB4 labels endothelial cells of blood vessels, providing a clear reference for spatial analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody against TH (1:100 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:200 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with IB4 (1:100 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-IgG (1:200 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for high-fat tissues like white adipose tissue due to its effective delipidation and dehydration steps that prevent lipid interference with optical clearing. It preserves fluorescence well, which is critical for detecting both TH-positive sympathetic nerve fibers and IB4-labeled peptidergic fibers. The use of DAPI allows nuclear labeling for structural reference, while the dual immunolabeling strategy enables clear distinction between adrenergic and peptidergic components. 1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Immunolabeling  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: anti-TH (1:500 in 1× PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100) and IB4 (1:100 in 1× PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 1× PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Alexa Fluor 555-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:500) in 1× PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 1× PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 in 1× PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
3.6 Incubation with 1× PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.6 Incubation with 1× PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ RI matching solution (1:1 v/v dibenzyl ether (DBE) in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

5.3 Incubation with fresh iDISCO+ RI matching solution (1:1 v/v DBE in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with 1× PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Mounting in iDISCO+ RI matching solution in a glass-bottomed dish or custom chamber suitable for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-suited for large, complex tissues like the whole mouse placenta due to its efficient dehydration and delipidation steps, which enhance deep penetration of fluorescent probes. It provides excellent optical clarity and fluorescence preservation, especially for vascular structures. CD31 labels endothelial cells, lectin stains luminal surfaces of blood vessels, and DAPI marks nuclei, enabling simultaneous visualization of vascular architecture, functional lumen, and cellular distribution. This labeling strategy avoids background noise while ensuring high contrast in both the placental margin and core.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody: CD31 (PECAM1) at 1:100 dilution in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG at 1:200 dilution in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with lectin (e.g., Ulex europaeus agglutinin I) at 1:100 dilution in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.5 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG at 1:200 dilution in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Incubation with 1× PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 1× PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 1× PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing reagent (10% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether in PBS, RI = 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing reagent (20% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether in PBS, RI = 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing reagent (40% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether in PBS, RI = 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.4 Incubation with uDISCO clearing reagent (60% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether in PBS, RI = 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.5 Incubation with uDISCO clearing reagent (80% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether in PBS, RI = 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.6 Incubation with uDISCO clearing reagent (100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether, RI = 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Preservation and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (RI = 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Mounting in a refractive index-matched medium (e.g., 1.48 RI gel or immersion oil) for imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Hoechst 33342, DiI, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for whole organ clearing due to its organic solvent-based approach, which effectively clears large tissues while preserving fluorescence signals. It allows for deep penetration and high transparency, ideal for imaging the complex 3D architecture of the testis. Hoechst 33342 provides nuclear labeling for identifying cell layers and stages of spermatogenesis, DiI labels germ cells and can trace their spatial distribution along the seminiferous tubules, and Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 highlights F-actin in Sertoli cells and other structures, aiding in defining cellular boundaries and organization.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (1:1000 in 100% methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with DiI (1:1000 in 100% methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:100 in 100% methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Washing with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert-butyl alcohol (TBA) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) TBA (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) TBA (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (1:1 v/v TBA: dibenzyl ether, DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (1:1 v/v TBA: DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (1:1 v/v TBA: DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1:1 v/v DBE: 1,1,1,3,3-pentane) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1:1 v/v DBE: 1,1,1,3,3-pentane) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1:1 v/v DBE: 1,1,1,3,3-pentane) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mounting the cleared tissue in RI-matching solution on a glass slide using a coverslip sealed with nail polish or optical-grade adhesive.  
6.2 Imaging using light-sheet microscopy or confocal laser scanning microscopy with appropriate excitation/emission settings for Hoechst 33342 (UV/460 nm), DiI (549 nm), and Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 (633 nm).

Phalloidin aids in delineating the muscular layers, while DAPI provides nuclear contrast. 1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Labeling

2.2 Incubation with 1:500 dilution of IB4 lectin in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated Phalloidin in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of DAPI in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for long tubular tissues like the mouse colon due to its organic solvent-based clearing that effectively removes lipids and provides excellent fluorescence preservation. It allows for deep penetration of fluorescent signals, which is critical for visualizing both neuronal cell bodies and nerve fibers in the full thickness of the intestinal wall. DiI labels lipid-rich structures such as axons and myelin sheaths, while Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 highlights F-actin in nerve processes and cell bodies. Hoechst 33342 stains nuclei for identifying neural ganglia. This combination enables dual detection of neuron somata and fibers with low background and high specificity.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with DiI (1 µg/mL in DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:50 dilution in DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (1 µg/mL in DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (1:1 v/v DCM:1,2-dichloropropane) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (1:1 v/v DCM:1,2-dichloropropane) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (1:1 v/v DCM:1,2-dichloropropane) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**Chosen Method:** EyeCi  
**Chosen Labeling:** [IB4 (for vascular lumen), Brn3a (for retinal ganglion cells)]  
**Justification:** EyeCi is specifically optimized for whole eye clearing, preserving fluorescence and maintaining the structural integrity of delicate ocular tissues like the retina. It uses a methanol-based clearing approach that is compatible with lipid-soluble fluorescent dyes and antibodies, which is ideal for labeling both vascular lumens (using IB4) and retinal ganglion cells (using Brn3a). This method allows for high-resolution imaging of the retina in 3D using light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of IB4 Alexa Fluor 647 in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 1:500 dilution of anti-Brn3a antibody (e.g., Abcam ab12452) in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Wash with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Sigma-Aldrich D2916) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (EyeCi RI-matching reagent, 1.51 RI) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of Hoechst 33342 in RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) for nuclear counterstaining  
5.2 Wash with RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)  
5.3 Mount the cleared eye in RI-matching solution for imaging (e.g., light-sheet or confocal microscope)

1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.2 Incubation with 1:100 diluted anti-Ki67 antibody (Alexa Fluor 488 conjugated) in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Ki67 (MKI67) + Alexa Fluor 488, PCNA + Alexa Fluor 647, Hoechst 33342]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for small 3D brain organoids due to its compatibility with lipid-soluble fluorescent dyes and efficient clearing of small tissues. It preserves fluorescence well, which is critical for detecting both cell cycle (Ki67) and DNA replication (PCNA) markers. Hoechst 33342 provides a nuclear counterstain for total cell quantification and segmentation. The use of Alexa Fluor conjugated secondary antibodies ensures high signal-to-noise ratios and spectral separation for multiplexed imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Washing with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Washing with PBS for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
1.5 Incubation with Ki67 primary antibody (1:200 dilution in blocking buffer) overnight (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16–18 hours)  
1.6 Washing with PBS-T (0.1% Tween-20 in PBS) for 3 × 10 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
1.7 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated secondary antibody (1:500 dilution in blocking buffer) for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.8 Washing with PBS-T for 3 × 10 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
1.9 Incubation with PCNA primary antibody (1:200 dilution in blocking buffer) overnight (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16–18 hours)  
1.10 Washing with PBS-T for 3 × 10 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
1.11 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated secondary antibody (1:500 dilution in blocking buffer) for 2 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.12 Washing with PBS-T for 3 × 10 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
1.13 Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (1:10,000 dilution in PBS) for 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
1.14 Washing with PBS for 3 × 5 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (1:1 mix of dibenzyl ether (DBE) and tetrahydrofuran (THF)) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 RI Matching  
6.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ refractive index matching solution (1:1 mix of DBE and THF) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with iDISCO+ refractive index matching solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with iDISCO+ refractive index matching solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) iDISCO+ refractive index matching solution for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Mounting in iDISCO+ refractive index matching solution on a glass-bottom dish for imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed)

This labeling strategy allows simultaneous detection of DNA replication (PCNA) and cell proliferation (Ki67), along with nuclear localization via DAPI, enabling high-resolution 3D imaging of organoid structure and drug-induced changes in growth and integrity.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with 1:200 dilution of anti-Ki67 antibody in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 1:200 dilution of anti-PCNA antibody in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of DAPI in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Washing with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)

4 Imaging Preparation

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 (Hu C/D) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for small tissue samples like skin biopsies due to its rapid clearing process and excellent fluorescence preservation, which is critical for detecting faintly labeled IENFs. The use of PGP9.5 (Hu C/D) as a specific marker for intraepidermal nerve fibers ensures accurate identification and quantification, while DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for reference in epidermal thickness and layering. This method allows for high-resolution 3D imaging with light-sheet or confocal microscopes, aligning with the goal of continuous tracking of IENFs across the epidermis and dermis.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA + 10% normal goat serum in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody (PGP9.5, 1:500 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody (Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG, 1:500 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 dilution in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM again (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing reagent (1:1 ratio of DCM and dibenzyl ether (DBE)) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing reagent (1:2 ratio of DCM and DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing reagent (1:4 ratio of DCM and DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with final RI-matching solution (1:10 ratio of DCM and DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE again (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Mounting on a glass slide with a coverslip using RI-matched mounting medium (RI = 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Justification:** uDISCO is well-suited for small tissue samples like skin biopsies due to its rapid clearing time and compatibility with lipid-soluble fluorescent dyes. The use of Hu C/D / PGP9.5 (for IENF), CD31 (for vascular network), and Lectin (for endothelial cells) provides a multi-channel labeling strategy that allows for 3D co-localization analysis without introducing extraneous targets. Additionally, uDISCO’s organic solvent-based clearing helps reduce melanin interference by dissolving pigments more effectively than aqueous methods like CUBIC.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of Hu C/D / PGP9.5 antibody in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 1:500 dilution of CD31 antibody in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of Lectin (e.g., Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated) in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Washing with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (10% (vol/vol) DCM, 10% (vol/vol) THF, 80% (vol/vol) DME) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert-butyl alcohol (TBA) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.6 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (e.g., 80% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol/20% (vol/vol) benzyl benzoate, RI = 1.52) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, mCherry]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-suited for small, intact organisms like *C. elegans* due to its rapid clearing process, excellent fluorescence preservation, and compatibility with organic solvents that do not quench GFP or RFP signals. The use of endogenous EGFP and mCherry reporters eliminates the need for additional labeling steps, simplifying the protocol while maintaining high-resolution imaging capabilities for 3D reconstruction of neural structures.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (10% (vol/vol) DCM, 10% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF), 80% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (20% (vol/vol) DCM, 20% (vol/vol) THF, 60% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (30% (vol/vol) DCM, 30% (vol/vol) THF, 40% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (40% (vol/vol) DCM, 40% (vol/vol) THF, 20% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 RI Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (1.48 refractive index, e.g., benzyl alcohol/benzyl benzoate (BABB) 1:1) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount the cleared worm in RI-matched medium using a low-viscosity mounting medium compatible with BABB (e.g., 1% (vol/vol) polyvinyl alcohol in BABB)  
6.2 Ensure the sample is fully immersed and free of air bubbles for optimal light-sheet or confocal imaging.

The method also supports fine structural resolution of sub-cellular features like the neural ring and axonal pathways.

1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) uDISCO Clear in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) uDISCO Clear in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) uDISCO Clear in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Refractive Index Matching  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) uDISCO Clear in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) uDISCO Clear in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Sample Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
3.1 Transfer cleared sample to a glass-bottomed dish filled with 100% uDISCO Clear (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Cover with a coverslip and seal with nail polish or vacuum grease (Temperature: RT, Time: 0 hours)

**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin (Alexa Fluor 488), Myosin VIIa antibody (Alexa Fluor 647)]  
**Justification:** ClearSee is a water-based, non-toxic clearing method that is particularly suitable for small whole organisms like zebrafish larvae. It provides excellent optical transparency while preserving fluorescent signals, which is critical for observing fine structures such as F-actin-rich stereocilia and Myosin VIIa-expressing hair cells. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin without the need for antibodies, ensuring high specificity and signal clarity. Myosin VIIa is a well-established marker for hair cells in the lateral line, making it ideal for identifying and localizing these cells in both the head and trunk neuromasts.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) sucrose in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) sucrose in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) sucrose in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with 1% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 0.5% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated Phalloidin (1:100 dilution in PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Washing with PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with anti-Myosin VIIa antibody (1:200 dilution in PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: overnight)  
3.4 Washing with PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated secondary antibody (1:200 dilution in PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.6 Washing with PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)  

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with ClearSee reagent (1:1 vol ClearSee solution to tissue volume) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with ClearSee reagent (1:1 vol ClearSee solution to tissue volume) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (e.g., 80% glycerol in PBS, RI = 1.47) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mounting in RI-matching solution on a glass-bottom dish or coverslip (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed for imaging)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin (F-actin), tdTomato (side line nerve fiber)]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-suited for small whole organisms like zebrafish larvae due to its rapid clearing time, excellent fluorescence preservation, and compatibility with organic dyes and fluorescent proteins. Phalloidin effectively labels F-actin in hair cells, while tdTomato provides robust labeling of side line nerve fibers, enabling precise 3D analysis of spatial relationships between hair cells and neurons.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated Phalloidin in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 1:500 dilution of tdTomato antibody in PBS with 0.1% (wt/vol) BSA (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.3 Washing with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)

5 Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 10% (vol/vol) NMP, 80% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI, e.g., dibenzyl ether or custom RI solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mounting in RI-matching solution using a low-viscosity mounting medium (e.g., 1.48 RI) in a glass-bottom dish (Temperature: RT, Time: immediately before imaging)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, YFP, Calbindin-D28k, Lectin]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for whole plant tissues like Arabidopsis seedlings due to its compatibility with lipid-soluble fluorescent proteins (e.g., GFP/YFP) and its ability to preserve endogenous fluorescence. It allows deep penetration of light, which is essential for imaging both root and shoot structures. The use of Calbindin-D28k as a cell-specific marker and lectin for cell wall staining provides high-resolution structural context without interfering with the fluorescent signals. This method also supports long-term sample storage in RI-matched medium, ideal for confocal or light-sheet microscopy.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.6 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of Calbindin-D28k antibody in PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 1:500 dilution of Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated secondary antibody in PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with 1 µg/mL wheat germ agglutinin (WGA)-Alexa Fluor 594 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 1 µg/mL lectin (e.g., ConA or PNA) in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Washing with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (10% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (20% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (40% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.4 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (60% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.5 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (80% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.6 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Sample Storage/Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether containing 0.01% (wt/vol) NaN3 (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 week or until imaging)  
6.2 Imaging using confocal or light-sheet microscopy with appropriate excitation/emission settings for GFP, YFP, and Alexa Fluor 594/647.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin (Alexa Fluor 594), Phalloidin (Alexa Fluor 488), DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for thick tissues like skeletal muscle due to its high penetration depth and excellent fluorescence preservation, which is critical for maintaining the integrity of delicate structures such as neuromuscular junctions (NMJs). The use of alpha-bungarotoxin directly labels acetylcholine receptors on the postsynaptic membrane, while phalloidin stains F-actin in muscle fibers, providing structural context. DAPI labels nuclei for anatomical reference. This combination allows precise visualization of NMJ morphology, including receptor clustering, fragmentation, and spatial distribution along the muscle fiber.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of alpha-bungarotoxin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 594 in 1× PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of Phalloidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 in 1× PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of DAPI in 1× PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
2.4 Washing with 1× PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 10 minutes)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI, e.g., 1.48 RI mounting medium or custom mix of 70% (vol/vol) glycerol + 30% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mounting the cleared tissue in RI-matching solution on a glass slide with a coverslip (Temperature: RT, Time: immediately before imaging)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin, DiI, Phalloidin]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is well-suited for whole muscle tissues due to its compatibility with lipid-rich tissues and minimal tissue shrinkage. It uses organic solvents (e.g., THF, DMSO) that are less damaging to fluorescent proteins and dyes compared to aqueous-based clearing methods. This method preserves fluorescence effectively, which is critical for detecting alpha-bungarotoxin labeling of AChRs and DiI for axonal tracing. Phalloidin can be used to label F-actin in the postsynaptic membrane, enhancing contrast and structural detail. The use of DiI allows for retrograde labeling of motor neurons, enabling visualization of the entire motor nerve terminal.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Alpha-Bungarotoxin Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with alpha-bungarotoxin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% methanol containing 0.1% (wt/vol) BSA (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3 DiI Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with DiI (1:1000 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% methanol containing 0.1% (wt/vol) BSA (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Phalloidin Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with Phalloidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 594 (1:100 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% methanol containing 0.1% (wt/vol) BSA (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5 Delipidation  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 1:1 mixture of THF and DMSO (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DMSO (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with uDISCO RI-matching solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO in water, RI = 1.47) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with uDISCO RI-matching solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO in water, RI = 1.47) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with uDISCO RI-matching solution (10% (vol/vol) DMSO in water, RI = 1.47) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mount the cleared tissue in a glass-bottomed dish filled with uDISCO RI-matching solution (RI = 1.47)  
7.2 Cover with a coverslip and seal with nail polish or optical-grade adhesive  
7.3 Perform 3D imaging using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate excitation/emission settings for Alexa Fluor 488, 594, and DiI signals

2.1 Incubation with 1:500 dilution of HuC/D antibody in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 1:200 dilution of IB4 lectin in 100% methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

请根据该科学问题自行选择合适的荧光/标记策略，并基于所选标记样本选择匹配的组织透明方法。若限制范围内的核染料只能提供细胞核定位或配准参考，则不应替代活动依赖性神经元主标记。请仅输出 protocol，第 1 行写明所选荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [c-Fos (Npas4) antibody + Alexa Fluor 647, tdTomato (for neural circuit tracing), DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for whole organ clearing of fixed tissues, including both brain and peripheral structures like the tongue. It provides excellent fluorescence preservation, especially for activity-dependent markers like c-Fos (Npas4), which are critical for identifying activated neurons during anesthesia and wakefulness. The use of tdTomato allows for long-term neural circuit tracing, while DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for anatomical reference. This method supports large tissue volumes and is compatible with light-sheet microscopy, ideal for 3D reconstruction of the tongue-brain neural loop.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum in PBS-T (0.1% Triton X-100) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody against c-Fos/Npas4 (1:500 dilution in PBS-T) for 2 days (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500 dilution in PBS-T) for 1 day (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 dilution in PBS) for 30 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI, e.g., SeeDB2 or custom mix of 1.48 RI oil) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) glycerol in RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM again (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP (primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 647), Neurofilament 200 (NF200, primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 488), DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for clearing large tissue blocks like scWAT due to its high penetration and compatibility with lipid-soluble reagents, which preserves fluorescence signals effectively. It allows for long-term storage of cleared samples in RI-matched media, ideal for multi-channel imaging. The labeling strategy includes specific markers for CGRP-positive sensory fibers (CGRP) and general neural networks (NF200), along with DAPI for nuclear counterstaining. This enables precise 3D quantification of sensory fiber density, branching, and coverage relative to the overall neural network.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% NGS + 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CGRP (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) and anti-NF200 (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) × 3 times  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-goat (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) × 3 times  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (10% (vol/vol) DCM, 10% (vol/vol) DBE, 80% (vol/vol) PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (100% (vol/vol) DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Final RI Matching and Storage  
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ mounting medium (RI = 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with fresh iDISCO+ mounting medium (RI = 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) × 3 times  
6.3 Mounting on glass slide with iDISCO+ mounting medium (RI = 1.48) for light-sheet or confocal imaging.

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (tyrosine hydroxylase), NPY, Lectin, Hoechst 33342]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for mineralized tissues like bone, offering excellent clearing efficiency while preserving fluorescent signals in both the calcified bone matrix and the soft bone marrow. It uses a methanol-based clearing agent with high refractive index (RI) matching, which is compatible with long-wavelength fluorophores such as those used for TH and NPY immunostaining. The use of Lectin for vascular labeling and Hoechst for nuclear staining provides a multi-channel approach suitable for 3D imaging of complex structures like bone marrow microenvironments.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum + 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: TH (1:500, rabbit polyclonal), NPY (1:200, mouse monoclonal) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies: anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 594 (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with biotinylated Lectin (1:100, Sigma L1301) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with streptavidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (1:1000) in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM again (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with BoneClear reagent (100% vol/vol, RI = 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with BoneClear reagent again (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (1.51, e.g., 100% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol + 10% (vol/vol) polyethylene glycol 400) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with RI matching solution again (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mounting sample in RI matching solution using a low-adhesion chamber or coverslip  
6.2 Imaging using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate excitation/emission settings for Alexa Fluor 488, 594, 647, and Hoechst 33342.

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH, NPY, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for mineralized bone tissues and preserves the structural integrity of both the dense cortical bone and the marrow cavity. It allows for deep penetration of antibodies and fluorescent probes, which is essential for detecting TH and NPY in the complex 3D architecture of the bone marrow microenvironment. The use of DAPI ensures nuclear labeling with minimal background, while avoiding additional fluorophores that may interfere with signal detection. This method supports high-resolution imaging of dual signals without requiring extensive decalcification, which could disrupt the bone structure.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethylene glycol (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Permeabilization with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Blocking with 5% (wt/vol) BSA in PBS-T (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200 dilution), anti-NPY (1:200 dilution) in PBS-T + 1% BSA (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.4 Washing with PBS-T (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)  
2.5 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-IgG (1:500 dilution), Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-IgG (1:500 dilution) in PBS-T + 1% BSA (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Washing with PBS-T (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 15 minutes)  
2.7 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 dilution) in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
2.8 Washing with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 5 minutes)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (1.48 RI, e.g., 80% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Preservation and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Mounting in RI-matched solution using a low-RI coverslip or custom chamber (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed for imaging)  
4.2 Imaging using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate excitation/emission settings for Alexa Fluor 488, 594, and DAPI.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin-Alexa Fluor 594, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for clearing large tissue samples like the mouse pancreas (12 mm × 8 mm × 5 mm) due to its high penetration depth and compatibility with lipid-soluble fluorescent dyes. It preserves fluorescence effectively, which is critical for visualizing fine neural structures such as axons and nerve fibers. The labeling strategy includes alpha-bungarotoxin for nicotinic acetylcholine receptors on motor neurons, Phalloidin for F-actin in axonal bundles, and DAPI for nuclear counterstaining. This combination allows precise visualization of both the neural network and tumor boundaries, enabling analysis of perineural invasion (PNI) patterns.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of alpha-bungarotoxin-Alexa Fluor 594 in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of DAPI in 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Wash  
3.1 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Preservation/Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with 100% DBE containing 0.1% (wt/vol) Sudan Black B (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Transfer to a glass-bottomed dish or imaging chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for whole organ clearing of fixed tissues like pancreatic tumors due to its high fluorescence preservation and compatibility with lipid-soluble fluorescent dyes. It allows for deep tissue penetration and is compatible with multi-channel imaging. The labeling strategy includes α-bungarotoxin for pan-neuronal staining, IB4 for sensory neurons, and CK19 for tumor epithelial boundaries, enabling precise spatial analysis of neural subpopulations relative to tumor architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of α-bungarotoxin-Alexa Fluor 594 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 1:1000 dilution of IB4-Alexa Fluor 488 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with 1:100 dilution of CK19 (导管)-Alexa Fluor 647 antibody in PBS with 0.3% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.4 Washing with PBS containing 0.3% Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

5 Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

6 RI Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) refractive index matching solution (RI = 1.48, e.g., SeeDB2 or custom oil) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

7 Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Mounting the cleared tissue in RI-matching solution within a glass-bottomed dish or custom chamber suitable for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.  
7.2 Ensure no air bubbles are present under the tissue.  
7.3 Store at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging.

3.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Labeling with tdTomato/RFP and E-cadherin

5.2 Incubation with secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200 dilution in DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Washing with DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

6 RI Matching and Final Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Imaging Preparation

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP (primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 647), TH (primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 594), DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for clearing mineralized tissues like bone due to its organic solvent-based delipidation and dehydration steps, which effectively penetrate dense structures. It preserves fluorescence well, allowing for deep penetration of antibodies into the bone marrow cavity and bone matrix. The use of specific primary antibodies against CGRP and TH, conjugated with high-contrast fluorescent dyes, enables clear distinction between sensory and sympathetic nerve fibers. DAPI is used for nuclear labeling to aid in structural reference during 3D imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert-butyl alcohol (TBA) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA in TBA) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: CGRP (1:100 dilution in TBA) + TH (1:100 dilution in TBA) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days with gentle shaking)  
3.3 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:200 dilution in TBA) + Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:200 dilution in TBA) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days with gentle shaking)  
3.4 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 dilution in TBA) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Incubation with TBA (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with TBA (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with TBA (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI, e.g., dibenzyl ether or custom mix) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Incubation with 1% (vol/vol) Sudan Black B in RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) to reduce background autofluorescence  
6.2 Incubation with fresh RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Mounting in RI-matching solution for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato, Sox10 (antibody), DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for small tissue samples like E9.5–E10.5 mouse embryos due to its rapid clearing process, excellent fluorescence preservation, and compatibility with lipid-soluble fluorescent proteins such as tdTomato. The method allows for deep penetration of light, which is essential for high-resolution 3D imaging of neural crest migration pathways. The use of DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for tissue structure reference, while Sox10 immunostaining enables specific identification of neural crest-derived cells and their differentiation states.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA + 10% normal goat serum in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody against Sox10 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS + 0.1% Tween-20) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) × 3 times  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with washing buffer (PBS + 0.1% Tween-20) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour) × 3 times  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing reagent (1:1 mix of dibenzyl ether and 2,2’-thiodiethanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing reagent (1:1 mix of dibenzyl ether and 2,2’-thiodiethanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing reagent (1:1 mix of dibenzyl ether and 2,2’-thiodiethanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Final RI Matching and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI, e.g., 1.48 RI glycerol-based solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI, e.g., 1.48 RI glycerol-based solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI, e.g., 1.48 RI glycerol-based solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Imaging  
5.1 Mount the cleared sample in a glass-bottom dish filled with RI-matching solution (1.48 RI).  
5.2 Perform 3D confocal or light-sheet microscopy using appropriate excitation/emission settings for tdTomato (561 nm/577–620 nm), Alexa Fluor 647 (633 nm/650–700 nm), and DAPI (405 nm/420–470 nm).

The labeling strategy includes specific antibodies against PSD95 (a key postsynaptic scaffold protein) and Homer1 (a postsynaptic structural protein), along with MAP2 to visualize dendritic architecture, enabling precise spatial analysis of puncta density, co-localization, and dendritic layering.

1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (1% BSA + 10% normal goat serum in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: anti-PSD95 (1:200, Alexa Fluor 647), anti-Homer1 (1:200, Alexa Fluor 488), and anti-MAP2 (1:200, Alexa Fluor 568) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody (if needed, e.g., anti-rabbit/mouse IgG, Alexa Fluor 647/488/568) in blocking solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PSD95 (secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 647), Homer1 (secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 488), MAP2 (secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 568)]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for thick brain tissue blocks due to its high penetration and compatibility with multiple fluorescent labels, including antibodies. It provides excellent optical clarity and fluorescence preservation, which is essential for resolving fine structures like dendritic spines and synaptic puncta in 3D. The use of MAP2 as a structural marker ensures accurate delineation of dendritic architecture, while dual labeling of PSD95 and Homer1 allows precise identification of excitatory postsynaptic scaffolds. This combination supports the analysis of spatial relationships between synapses and dendritic morphology.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 10% normal goat serum (NGS) in PBS-Triton (PBST) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Primary Antibody Incubation  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies against PSD95 (1:500), Homer1 (1:500), and MAP2 (1:500) diluted in PBST + 1% NGS for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBST for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  

3 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor 647, 488, and 568 conjugated) at 1:500 dilution in PBST + 1% NGS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBST for 3 × 15 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Delipidation  
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (1:1:1 v/v/v mixture of DCM, 2-methoxyethanol, and dibasic sodium phosphate) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh iDISCO+ clearing solution for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (1:1:1 v/v/v mixture of DCM, 2-methoxyethanol, and dibasic sodium phosphate) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with fresh RI matching solution for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Mount the cleared tissue block in RI matching solution within a glass-bottomed dish or custom chamber suitable for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.  
8.2 Ensure no air bubbles are present under the tissue block before imaging.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Synapsin (for presynaptic markers), PSD-95 (for postsynaptic markers), Phalloidin (for F-Actin), DAPI (for nuclei)]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is well-suited for thick tissue blocks (1–2 mm) due to its high penetration and efficient clearing of large volumes. It preserves fluorescence well, especially for endogenous or antibody-labeled proteins like Synapsin and PSD-95, which are critical for identifying excitatory synapses. Phalloidin labels F-Actin in dendritic spines, aiding in spine density quantification, while DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining. The organic solvent-based clearing minimizes tissue deformation, ensuring structural integrity of dendrites and synaptic puncta.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Preparation
1.1 Incubation with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.2 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2 Immunolabeling
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Synapsin (1:500), anti-PSD-95 (1:500), and Phalloidin (1:100) in blocking buffer (10% NGS + 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 48 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.2 Wash with PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100 for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibodies (anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647, anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 568) in blocking buffer for 24 hours (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.4 Wash with PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100 for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.5 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000) in PBS for 30 minutes (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
2.6 Wash with PBS for 3 × 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3 Dehydration
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Delipidation
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 1 hour (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5 Clearing
5.1 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE)) for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
5.2 Incubation with iDISCO+ clearing solution (100% DBE) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6 Refractive Index Matching
6.1 Incubation with RI matching solution (1.51 RI, e.g., 100% (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol + 10% (vol/vol) benzyl benzoate) for 24 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

7 Imaging Preparation
7.1 Mount the cleared tissue block in RI matching solution on a glass slide using a coverslip.
7.2 Ensure no air bubbles are present under the coverslip.
7.3 Perform high-resolution confocal or light-sheet microscopy imaging immediately or store at 4 ℃ in RI matching solution for up to 7 days.

**Protocol Steps:**

1 Tissue Optical Clearing  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody against Cx40/Hcn4 (1:100 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with DiI (1 µg/mL in 100% methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:50 dilution in 100% methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Wash  
3.1 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

5.1 Incubation with RI-matching solution (1.48, e.g., SeeDB2 or custom glycerol-based solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

5.3 Incubation with RI-matching solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

6.1 Mounting the cleared heart in RI-matching solution within a glass-bottomed dish or imaging chamber (Temperature: RT, Time: as needed)
